\section[causar]{causar — to cause}

\label{lesson:ES-C581-causar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for seeing as, then the Spanish for given that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: causar}
\textbf{causar} — \textquotedblleft{}to cause\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La lluvia causó muchos problemas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The rain caused a lot of problems.}
\end{quote}

Regular -ar verb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{causar} is built on \emph{causa}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{causa} 'reason, cause' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{causar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{causar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{causar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for seeing as, then the Spanish for given that, then say \emph{causar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does causar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To cause\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[provocar]{provocar — to bring about, to cause; to provoke}

\label{lesson:ES-C581-provocar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for given that, then the Spanish for to cause.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: provocar}
\textbf{provocar} — \textquotedblleft{}to bring about, to cause; to provoke\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El ruido provoca dolor de cabeza.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Noise causes headaches.}
\end{quote}

Often for bad results: \emph{provocar un accidente}. Spelling: \emph{provoqué}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{provocar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{provocare} 'to call forth, to challenge', built from \emph{pro-} and \emph{vocare} 'to call' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{provocar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{provocar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{provocar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for given that, then the Spanish for to cause, then say \emph{provocar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does provocar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To bring about, to cause; to provoke\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[debido a]{debido a — due to, owing to}

\label{lesson:ES-C581-debido-a}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to cause, then the Spanish for to bring about.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: debido a}
\textbf{debido a} — \textquotedblleft{}due to, owing to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El tren llega tarde debido a la nieve.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The train arrives late due to the snow.}
\end{quote}

Followed by a noun: \emph{debido al frío}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{debido a} is built on \emph{debido}, the participle of \emph{deber}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{debere} 'to owe' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{debido a}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{debido a}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{debido a}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to cause, then the Spanish for to bring about, then say \emph{debido a} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does debido a mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Due to, owing to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a causa de]{a causa de — because of}

\label{lesson:ES-C581-a-causa-de}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to bring about, then the Spanish for due to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a causa de}
\textbf{a causa de} — \textquotedblleft{}because of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No salimos a causa del frío.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We did not go out because of the cold.}
\end{quote}

Followed by a noun; \emph{porque} is followed by a whole sentence.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{a causa de} is built on \emph{causa}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{causa} 'reason, cause' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a causa de}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a causa de}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a causa de}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to bring about, then the Spanish for due to, then say \emph{a causa de} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a causa de mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Because of\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[gracias a]{gracias a — thanks to}

\label{lesson:ES-C581-gracias-a}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for due to, then the Spanish for because of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: gracias a}
\textbf{gracias a} — \textquotedblleft{}thanks to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Aprobé gracias a tu ayuda.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I passed thanks to your help.}
\end{quote}

For a good cause; for a bad one people say \emph{por culpa de}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gracias a} is built on \emph{gracias}, the plural of \emph{gracia}, inherited from Latin \emph{gratia} 'favour, thanks' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gracias a}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gracias a}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gracias a}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for due to, then the Spanish for because of, then say \emph{gracias a} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does gracias a mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Thanks to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
